title: Reduced Cost Quantum Kernel Training
summary: Quantum kernel methods are promising for near-term quantum machine learning, but their training costs are driven by the quadratic scaling of Gram-matrix construction and the measurement cost of estimating individual kernel values. In this work, we investigate one-class anomaly detection as a resource-efficient operating regime for training non-variational quantum kernel models. Using the ULB Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset, we evaluate three quantum feature maps across training-set sizes and qubit counts.
